title: Product Chunking That Answers
objective: After this lesson you will be able to chunk catalogs by question boundaries (per-variant units), attach SKU/category/price/version metadata, and verify chunk answerability with gold probes before indexing anything.
why: Generic fixed-size chunking shreds product semantics: a variant's price lands three chunks from its size chart, and no retrieval recovers the pairing. Product questions target variants, policies target clauses, comparisons target rows — chunk boundaries must follow question boundaries, with metadata carrying everything filters, citations, and freshness need.

blocks.text: Ask what shoppers ask, then cut there: **per-variant units** (size/color/price answers live at variant grain), **per-clause policy chunks** (one rule + its exceptions together), **per-row spec tables** (comparisons need aligned rows). Fixed-character chunking is the fallback when structure is absent — never the default on structured catalogs. A chunk should answer its question class alone, without assembly.

blocks.caption: Structure-aware units with complete provenance per chunk

blocks.text: Every chunk carries: **identity** (sku/id for citations), **category** (filtering), **price + version + updated** (freshness/staleness), **kind** (variant vs policy vs review — different handling). Missing metadata fails silently downstream: unfilterable, uncitable, unfreshenable. The metadata schema is reviewed like a DB schema — because it is one.

Before embedding anything, prove chunks answer: take 10 real questions, require each answer's facts present **in one chunk** (or explicitly adjacent pair). Failures redesign boundaries (split merged topics, merge scattered facts) — chunking iterates on probes, never aesthetics. Indexing unprobed chunks is hoping at scale.

blocks.title: Chunk and probe
blocks.note: Run it: expect 2 units with variant ids, the size-9 price self-contained in one chunk, and full metadata. Answerability proven per question class before any embedding happens.

items: Cut at question boundaries (variants, clauses, rows) — fixed-size is the fallback, never the default
Metadata (sku/category/price/version/updated/kind) enables filtering, citations, freshness — schema-reviewed
Answerability probes gate indexing: each question class answerable in ≤1 chunk or boundaries redesign

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice chunker and confirm units/ids/answerability/metadata. (b) Add the policy chunk (returns + warranty with kind+version metadata) and re-run. (c) Write two answerability probes (variant price; return window) stating the chunk each must hit — then confirm both hit.
hints: Baseline: 2 units, SH-1-v8/SH-1-v9 ids, size-9 self-contained, metadata complete.
Policy chunk: id SH-1-policy, kind policy, version/updated carried — third unit, same guarantees.
Probes assert single-chunk containment: price→variant unit, window→policy unit. Scattered facts fail probes by design.
exercise.why: Answerability-driven chunking (probes before indexes, boundaries from questions, metadata as schema) is the unit economics of RAG: every downstream stage inherits these decisions.
exercise.code: // Probe pattern: question → required facts → assert single-chunk containment.

quiz.q: Size-9 price needs three chunks assembled. Problem?
options: Boundary failure: variant questions need variant-grain units — redesign cuts, don't assemble at query time
quiz.explain: Assembly-at-query is fragile composition. Question-grain units answer alone; probes enforce it pre-index.

options: Unfreshenable: staleness checks, recency ranking, and price guards all need dates — metadata gaps fail silently downstream
quiz.explain: Metadata is load-bearing infrastructure for filtering, citations, and freshness. Missing fields fail downstream invisibly.

quiz.q: Fixed 500-char chunks on a structured catalog. Verdict?
options: Fallback thinking: structure-aware cuts (variants/clauses/rows) first; fixed-size only where structure is absent
quiz.explain: Structure carries semantics fixed sizes shred. Cut with the grain (questions), fall back to characters only unstructured.

summary: Question-grain units, complete metadata, probe-gated indexing. Chunks are answers waiting for questions — design them as such.
next: Units built — now make them findable: embeddings, similarity, and honest baselines. Next: meaning as vectors.
